initiatives.name: Financial Services Phased Withdrawal
initiatives.summary: Sainsbury's is executing a phased withdrawal from its Financial Services (banking) business, transferring assets and operations to NatWest, NewDay, and NoteMachine. This transition reduces the Group's exposure to credit, liquidity, and capital adequacy risks associated with running a bank.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £52 million cash outflow for Financial Services strategic review; Financial Services phased withdrawal costs of £133 million (2025) and £245 million (2024)

evidence.title: NewDay Acquires Argos Financial Services Portfolio
evidence.summary: As part of the Financial Services phased withdrawal, NewDay acquired beneficial title to the Argos Financial Services portfolio in February 2025. This is part of the broader distributed model transition for Sainsbury's Bank operations.
evidence.quote: in February 2025, NewDay acquired beneficial title to the Argos Financial Services portfolio.

evidence.title: Financial Services Divestment to NatWest, NewDay, NoteMachine
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's is executing a phased withdrawal from its Financial Services (banking) business, transferring assets and operations to NatWest, NewDay, and NoteMachine. This transition reduces the Group's exposure to credit, liquidity, and capital adequacy risks associated with running a bank.
evidence.quote: Good progress has been made in transitioning Financial Services to a distributed model, with assets and operations being transferred to NatWest, NewDay, and NoteMachine. This transition has reduced the risk profile. The sale of banking operations to NatWest is currently in progress and subject to regulatory approval.

evidence.title: Joint Oversight Committee for Financial Services Strategy
evidence.summary: A Joint Oversight Committee including Group and Bank representation has been established to guide the execution of the new Financial Services strategy, reflecting a governance change to manage the Bank's transition.
evidence.quote: A Joint Oversight Committee including Group and Bank representation has been established to guide execution of the new Financial Services strategy

initiatives.name: Fleet Electrification and Charging Infrastructure
initiatives.summary: Sainsbury's completed a successful trial with long-term produce supplier Strawson's using electric HGVs to explore moving away from fossil fuels in produce supply chains, and has agreed a further rollout following the trial's success.

evidence.title: Electric HGV Trial with Produce Supplier Strawson's
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's completed a successful trial with long-term produce supplier Strawson's using electric HGVs to explore moving away from fossil fuels in produce supply chains, and has agreed a further rollout following the trial's success.
evidence.quote: This year we also completed a trial with Strawson's, one of our long-term produce suppliers, on the use of electric HGVs to explore the feasibility of moving away from fossil fuel use in our produce supply chains, agreeing a further rollout following a successful trial.

evidence.title: Grid Scale Battery and EV Truck Charger Network at Distribution Centres
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's is preparing to install a grid scale battery system at a distribution centre in Spring 2026 to trial balancing electricity consumption with the grid, alongside developing a network of EV truck chargers going live in 2026 to support the introduction of its first electric trucks.
evidence.quote: Preparations were made for the installation of a grid scale battery system in one of our distribution centres in Spring 2026, to trial how the technology can support the site in balancing its electricity consumption with the grid. We also continued to work on the development of a network of EV truck chargers that will go live in 2026 as we look to introduce our first electric trucks into our fleet.

evidence.title: Fleet Electrification and Depot Charging Infrastructure
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's made a significant investment in 2024 installing electric plug points across ten depots, enabling its full fleet of 450 rigid vehicles to charge refrigeration units via 100% renewable electricity. The company is also expanding EV vans in its Groceries Online operations to over 200 vehicles and introduced 30 biomethane HGVs.
evidence.quote: We also made a significant investment in 2024 across ten of our depots by installing electric plug points for our rigid fleet, enabling our full fleet of 450 rigids to charge their refrigeration units via 100 per cent renewable electricity whilst stationary at our depots.

initiatives.name: Next Level Sainsbury's Strategy
initiatives.summary: A three-year restructuring programme was commenced to update central management structures at Sainsbury's and Argos, creating fewer, bigger roles with clearer accountabilities to support faster decision-making. This is part of the Next Level Sainsbury's strategy announced in February 2024.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £62 million costs incurred in current year, £31 million cash costs; total cash costs of around £150 million expected

evidence.title: Next Level Sainsbury's Strategy - First Choice for Food
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's committed to its 'Next Level Sainsbury's' strategy aiming to become the 'First choice for food' by expanding its food range to more customers, targeting grocery market volume share gains and profit leverage from sales growth.
evidence.quote: We've committed to become the First choice for food by bringing more of Sainsbury's food range to more customers. This will deliver further grocery market volume share gains and profit leverage from sales growth

evidence.title: Next Level Sainsbury's Strategy Restructuring Programme
evidence.summary: A three-year restructuring programme was commenced to update central management structures at Sainsbury's and Argos, creating fewer, bigger roles with clearer accountabilities to support faster decision-making. This is part of the Next Level Sainsbury's strategy announced in February 2024.
evidence.quote: as part of our Next Level Sainsbury's strategy implementation announced in February 2024, we have commenced a three-year restructuring programme which will update our central management structures to support faster decision-making and drive performance at both Sainsbury's and Argos, creating fewer, bigger roles with clearer accountabilities.

evidence.title: Closure of Food Counters, Cafés, and Bakery Conversions
evidence.summary: As part of the Next Level Sainsbury's strategy, the company announced consultation on closing food counters and cafés, and converting remaining scratch bakeries. This forms part of the broader simplification and cost reduction restructuring effort.
evidence.quote: As part of the strategy, it was also announced in the current year that we will be consulting on the closure of food counters, cafés, and the conversion of remaining scratch bakeries.

initiatives.name: 2020 Multi-Year Restructuring Programme
initiatives.summary: A multi-year restructuring programme announced in November 2020 has largely completed, with cumulative costs incurred of £907 million and cumulative cash costs of £310 million to date. This reflects a long-running cost reduction and simplification effort.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £907 million cumulative costs, £310 million cumulative cash costs

evidence.title: 2020 Multi-Year Restructuring Programme Nearing Completion
evidence.summary: A multi-year restructuring programme announced in November 2020 has largely completed, with cumulative costs incurred of £907 million and cumulative cash costs of £310 million to date. This reflects a long-running cost reduction and simplification effort.
evidence.quote: Most of the 2020 programme has now completed, with costs incurred to date of £907 million, and cash costs to date of £310 million.

initiatives.name: Highbury and Dragon Property Transaction
initiatives.summary: The Group completed a significant property transaction (Highbury and Dragon) in the prior year, involving net consideration paid of £670 million and associated non-cash lease movements, reflecting portfolio and real estate restructuring.

evidence.title: Highbury and Dragon Property Transaction

initiatives.name: EV Charging Infrastructure Investment
initiatives.summary: Sainsbury's made a strategic investment in electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure, though the amount decreased year-on-year, indicating this is a continuing but scaling-down sustainability-linked capital programme.

evidence.title: EV Charging Infrastructure Investment
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's made a strategic investment in electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure, though the amount decreased year-on-year, indicating this is a continuing but scaling-down sustainability-linked capital programme.
evidence.quote: Strategic investment in electric vehicles (EV) charging infrastructure was £25 million (2023/24: £63 million).

initiatives.name: Project Graphite Energy Efficiency Programme
initiatives.summary: Sainsbury's completed its 15th year of Project Graphite, a dedicated capital investment programme focused on decarbonisation of heat, renewable energy, and energy efficiency technology trials. This year alone the company spent £18 million on the programme covering controller trials, enhanced metering, remote monitoring, and battery technologies.

evidence.title: Project Graphite Energy Efficiency Programme
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's completed its 15th year of Project Graphite, a dedicated capital investment programme focused on decarbonisation of heat, renewable energy, and energy efficiency technology trials. This year alone the company spent £18 million on the programme covering controller trials, enhanced metering, remote monitoring, and battery technologies.
evidence.quote: This year, through Graphite (our energy efficiency investment programme), we have spent £18 million focused on the decarbonisation of heat, increasing the amount of renewable energy, energy efficiency and technology trials as we continue to focus on engineering innovation, which supports identification of the latest technology to support our decarbonisation roadmap.

initiatives.name: Net Zero Emissions and SBTi Alignment
initiatives.summary: Sainsbury's has SBTi-approved 1.5°C aligned targets to reach net zero in its own operations by 2035 and across its Scope 3 value chain emissions by 2050. The company has already achieved a 53.6% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions from its 2018/19 baseline.

evidence.title: Net Zero Targets for Scope 1, 2 and 3 Emissions
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's has SBTi-approved 1.5°C aligned targets to reach net zero in its own operations by 2035 and across its Scope 3 value chain emissions by 2050. The company has already achieved a 53.6% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions from its 2018/19 baseline.
evidence.quote: We have a Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) 1.5°C aligned target to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions to net zero within our own operations by 2035 and in our Scope 3 emissions by 2050.

initiatives.name: Smart Charge EV Charging Business
initiatives.summary: Sainsbury's launched a dedicated electric vehicle charging business, Smart Charge, in 2024, giving customers access to ultra-rapid EV charging points across its store estate as it responds to the transition away from petrol/diesel vehicles ahead of the 2035 ban.

evidence.title: Smart Charge EV Charging Business Launch
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's launched a dedicated electric vehicle charging business, Smart Charge, in 2024, giving customers access to ultra-rapid EV charging points across its store estate as it responds to the transition away from petrol/diesel vehicles ahead of the 2035 ban.
evidence.quote: Following the launch of our dedicated electric vehicle (EV) charging business, Smart Charge, in 2024, our customers can now access 661 ultra-rapid EV charging points across 80 Sainsbury's stores.

initiatives.name: La Celia Lower Carbon Coffee Partnership
initiatives.summary: Sainsbury's partnered with coffee supplier La Celia to launch a new lower carbon coffee range, using low emission fertilisation and forest restoration while supporting women farmers in Colombia. The dedicated roast and ground product launched in July 2025.

evidence.title: Strategic Partnership with La Celia Coffee Suppliers
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's partnered with coffee supplier La Celia to launch a new lower carbon coffee range, using low emission fertilisation and forest restoration while supporting women farmers in Colombia. The dedicated roast and ground product launched in July 2025.
evidence.quote: During the year we partnered with our coffee supplier to launch a new coffee range from La Celia... In July 2025, we launched a dedicated roast and ground coffee product from La Celia, Colombia, producing lower ca[rbon coffee]

initiatives.name: Technology, Supply Chain and Logistics Capex Programme
initiatives.summary: Cash capital expenditure increased year-on-year to £825 million, driven primarily by increased investment in technology, supply chain and logistics. The Group expects core retail capex of £800-850 million in 2025/26.

evidence.title: Increased Technology, Supply Chain and Logistics Investment
evidence.summary: Cash capital expenditure increased year-on-year to £825 million, driven primarily by increased investment in technology, supply chain and logistics. The Group expects core retail capex of £800-850 million in 2025/26.
evidence.quote: Cash capital expenditure was £825 million (2023/24: £814 million). The year‑on-year increase was primarily driven by increased investment in technology, supply chain and logistics.

initiatives.name: Save and Invest to Win Cost Savings
initiatives.summary: The company operates a cost savings programme ('Save and to invest to win') targeting significant annual savings, with delivery risk explicitly modeled as capable of causing c.£100 million annual cost impact if delayed. Cumulative cost savings targets of £800m-£1,000m are used as LTIP performance metrics.

evidence.title: Save and Invest to Win Cost Savings Programme
evidence.summary: The company operates a cost savings programme ('Save and to invest to win') targeting significant annual savings, with delivery risk explicitly modeled as capable of causing c.£100 million annual cost impact if delayed. Cumulative cost savings targets of £800m-£1,000m are used as LTIP performance metrics.
evidence.quote: Delays in delivering the Save and to invest to win programme, which would have an impact of c. £100 million in each year of the assessment period, were considered.

initiatives.name: £550 Million Investment Grade Bond Issuance
initiatives.summary: In January 2025, the Group issued £550 million of Investment Grade Corporate Bonds, alongside repaying a £575 million committed term loan facility, as part of financing strategy to support liquidity and capital structure.

evidence.title: £550 million Investment Grade Corporate Bond Issuance
evidence.summary: In January 2025, the Group issued £550 million of Investment Grade Corporate Bonds, alongside repaying a £575 million committed term loan facility, as part of financing strategy to support liquidity and capital structure.
evidence.quote: In January 2025 the Group issued £550 million of Investment Grade Corporate Bonds.

initiatives.name: Egg Supply Chain Transition to White Eggs
initiatives.summary: Sainsbury's is transitioning its shell eggs from brown to white eggs across own brand core ranges, aiming for 100% transition, as white eggs are less carbon intensive and deliver higher animal welfare outcomes.

evidence.title: Egg Supply Chain Transition from Brown to White Eggs
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's is transitioning its shell eggs from brown to white eggs across own brand core ranges, aiming for 100% transition, as white eggs are less carbon intensive and deliver higher animal welfare outcomes.
evidence.quote: We are making progress on transitioning our shell eggs from brown to white eggs, which are less carbon intensive and result in higher animal welfare outcomes, aiming towards 100 per cent in our own brand core ranges.

initiatives.name: Phased Withdrawal from Financial Services
initiatives.summary: Sainsbury's is undergoing a phased withdrawal from its Financial Services banking business, with the company noting that climate-related risk exposure for the Bank is now deemed immaterial given its reduced size and lack of mortgage or corporate lending portfolios.

evidence.title: Phased Withdrawal from Financial Services
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's is undergoing a phased withdrawal from its Financial Services banking business, with the company noting that climate-related risk exposure for the Bank is now deemed immaterial given its reduced size and lack of mortgage or corporate lending portfolios.
evidence.quote: Given the phased withdrawal from Financial Services and the size of the Bank in relation to the Group, we deem the climate-related impacts to be immaterial.

initiatives.name: Environmental Risk Mapping and Supplier Resilience
initiatives.summary: Sainsbury's is expanding an environmental risk assessment programme across sourcing regions using eight risk indicators, feeding into commercial reviews and supplier contracts. The company is building a centralised data platform for environmental and supply risk analytics to strengthen long-term supply resilience.

evidence.title: Environmental Risk Mapping and Supplier Resilience Programme
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's is expanding an environmental risk assessment programme across sourcing regions using eight risk indicators, feeding into commercial reviews and supplier contracts. The company is building a centralised data platform for environmental and supply risk analytics to strengthen long-term supply resilience.
evidence.quote: Looking ahead, we are expanding this work through a more integrated, forward-looking resilience programme that focuses on enhancing supplier relationships, developing a centralised data platform for environmental and supply risk analytics and building capability across internal teams.

initiatives.name: TCFD and TNFD Climate and Nature Disclosures
initiatives.summary: Sainsbury's became an early adopter of the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) in addition to complying with TCFD requirements under FCA Listing Rule LR 6.6.6(8), aiming to build out nature-related disclosure and quantify impacts over time.

evidence.title: TCFD and TNFD Aligned Climate and Nature Disclosures
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's became an early adopter of the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) in addition to complying with TCFD requirements under FCA Listing Rule LR 6.6.6(8), aiming to build out nature-related disclosure and quantify impacts over time.
evidence.quote: We have complied with the Financial Conduct Authority Listing Rule LR 6.6.6(8) by including climate-related financial disclosures consistent with all of the TCFD recommendations which we discuss below.

initiatives.name: Net Zero by 2035 and Plan for Better
initiatives.summary: Sainsbury's has committed to becoming net zero in its own operations by 2035, embedding this within its Plan for Better sustainability strategy which includes emissions reduction, packaging reduction, and energy usage reduction across the estate.

evidence.title: Net Zero by 2035 and Plan for Better Commitments
evidence.summary: Sainsbury's has committed to becoming net zero in its own operations by 2035, embedding this within its Plan for Better sustainability strategy which includes emissions reduction, packaging reduction, and energy usage reduction across the estate.
evidence.quote: Net zero – our commitment to becoming net zero in our own operations by 2035 through reducing our GHG emissions as much as possible and not adding to the amount of GHG in the atmosphere.
